messages:
pagerbot: PagerDuty alert triggered: HIGH CPU+GPU queue growth on cluster-gpu-prod (P1). 120s sustained queue increase. Trigger: gpu-queue-length > 90% for 3m. Escalating to oncall-sre and infra.

Sam (oncall-sre): I'm on it. seeing a massive backlog on the render-llm queue, ingress rate fine. autoscaler events show repeated 'attach instance profile failed' for ng-gpu-1.

Priya (ops-lead): Customer-impact? any active customer errors?

Maya (cust-success): A handful of customers on low-latency tier reported timeouts ~5m ago, dashboard shows many generation requests 503 from our gateway.

Sam (oncall-sre): Logs ->
```
Autoscaler: failed to create instance in nodegroup ng-gpu-1: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::1234567890:role/redwood-gpu-node-role
```

Sam (oncall-sre): Looks IAM attach role failing during launchTemplate apply. launch template version v12 references instance profile arn:...:gpu-profile-v2; nodegroup's instanceProfile expects gpu-profile-v1. mismatch.

Diego (eng-runtime): That'll block new GPU nodes; autoscaler tries but AWS rejects. Can we fallback to warm-pool or dedicated spare nodes?

Kai (infra): Warm pool is empty; reserved Dedicated capacity saturated. We have two quick options: 1) temporarily relax queue throttle and send traffic to cpu-only fallback model (lower perf) or 2) manually create nodes with a corrected launch template and attach taints/labels. Manual will take ~10–15m to come up.

Priya (ops-lead): Prioritize minimizing customer errors. Jordan, can runtime route requests to cpu-fallback?

Jordan (eng-oncall): Yes, can flip routing policy to prefer cpu-fallback for non-SLA customers. Need a PR and a config rollout, can do a fast feature-flag toggle. Will take ~6m to propagate.

Sam (oncall-sre): I'm going to attempt manual nodegroup create with corrected instance profile and taint config. I'll run the command and attach logs here. If that fails, we escalate to infra.

Kai (infra): FYI, we also saw an odd taint propagation bug where kubelet didn't apply gpu=present:NoSchedule until the node had the latest kube-proxy image. That's separate but could cause pods to not land even if node is provisioned. I'll prepare a patched launch template that pins the AMI and kube-proxy version.

Sam (oncall-sre): running create command:
```
aws eks create-nodegroup --cluster-name cluster-gpu-prod --nodegroup-name ng-gpu-urgent-1 \
  --node-role arn:aws:iam::1234567890:role/redwood-gpu-node-role-v2 \
  --launch-template name=lt-gpu,version=13 --scaling-config minSize=0,maxSize=10,desiredSize=4
```

Sam (oncall-sre): aws response -> creation accepted. CloudFormation stack in progress.

Diego (eng-runtime): Jordan, start the route flip to cpu-fallback for non-SLA now. Leave high-tier customers pinned to gpu models.

Jordan (eng-oncall): toggled feature-flag: routing.fallback.cpu=true (rollout ids: ff/382). Monitoring.

Maya (cust-success): I've messaged top impacted customers with ETA ~15-30m and temporary mitigation (retries + cpu fallback note). They're ok for now but want updates.

Sam (oncall-sre): Stack events: ASG creation succeeded, instances launching but cloud-init errors on one instance:
```
cloud-init[123]: ERROR: failed to attach instance profile: InvalidInstanceProfile. Expected arn:...:gpu-profile-v2
```

Sam (oncall-sre): Looks like LT still referencing old instance profile in one of the template overrides. Rolling back and updating launch template version to v14 to ensure correct profile and kube-proxy pinned.

Kai (infra): I've pushed lt v14 with corrected iam instance profile and user-data fix for taint application. Recommend forcing a re-create of the problematic nodes after they finish booting.

Sam (oncall-sre): forcing nodegroup replace now (terminate failing instances, let ASG reprovision).

Sam (oncall-sre): New instances boot healthy, kubelet registered, taints applied. kubectl get nodes shows 4 new gpu nodes ready.

Diego (eng-runtime): autoscaler now shows desired=10 but current=9, will rebalance. Queue depth trending down from 95% to 30% over last 4m. Latency on the gateway back to normal for SLA customers. Non-SLA on cpu-fallback still at slightly higher latency but stable.

Priya (ops-lead): Great. Next steps: post-incident: update runbook to include launch template ver check before ASG autoscale, add a preflight that validates iam:PassRole for nodegroup principal, and add warm-pool sizing for peak windows. Sam/Kai/Jordan owners?

Sam (oncall-sre): I'll own runbook updates for nodegroup rollout checklist.

Kai (infra): I'll add CI job to validate launch template instance profile matches expected role and pin kube-proxy AMI.

Jordan (eng-oncall): I'll extend routing flags to support graceful degradation tiers and document flip procedure.

Maya (cust-success): Noted — will follow up with customers with incident summary once SRE sends the RCA.

pagerbot: Incident downgraded to INCIDENT: mitigated. PagerDuty note: mitigation applied at 1725013200.

Sam (oncall-sre): marking this thread for postmortem. Will collect logs and timeline. If anyone has additional notes, paste here. :white_check_mark:
